newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila T-bill mkt on buying side after rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: Manila T-bill mkt on buying side after rate cuts.

text.p: Manila banks trekked back to the secondary Treasury bills market to buy bills after the successive reduction in central bank reverse repo rates, traders said.
However, they found no willing sellers.
"When the market moves, traders just move in one direction," a foreign bank dealer said.
Traders said banks have decided to position ahead of the further slide in interest rates.
The central bank on Thursday cut its overnight borrowing rate to 25 percent from 28 percent after the forex trading started to normalise from a de facto devaluation last week.
Banks had begun quoting lower rates for the three- and six-month bills, while rates for the one-year bills were steady despite higher demand.
A Reuters poll of five financial institutions gave bids of 13.30/14 percent for three-month bills; 14.25/14.75 percent for six months; and 15/16 percent for the one-year bills.
The average interbank call loan rate fell to 25.09375 percent from 28.1875 percent in line with the latest rate cut by the central bank.
Volume was lower at 9.05 billion pesos from 12.66 billion, with 30 lenders and 21 borrowers.
